Auction · Room. Goal: Finish with the highest total of coins, owned item values and reputation. Your turn: Eight actions. Bidding resolves the next lot; you may also post an indicative price, announce a bidding ceiling, or sponsor Bidder 1. Scoring: Lots are worth 4, 6 and 10. The highest sealed bid wins and pays its bid; a bid cannot exceed your bank. Each lot won earns a 3-coin commission. Indicative prices and ceilings are public talk, not bids. Sponsoring costs 1 coin and gives Bidder 1 reputation. If Bidder 1 finishes ahead of Bidder 2, you receive a 5-coin finder's fee. Rivals: A live player controls each other seat, choosing its actions from its own observations and the game history.
Round 3/8. Scores: [15, 15.0, 14.0].
Last resolution: Lot 2 (value 6): bids you 6, Bidder 1 5, Bidder 2 4. You won and paid 6; commission 3.

Bidder 1 has 11 coins and has bid aggressively, so a max bid either wins outright or forces them to pay 10+, capping their final score around 17-18 while I bank the 5-coin finder's fee since they'd stay ahead of Bidder 2. A low bid risks them winning cheap and running away with it.
